mission: Build a fractal Google Maps of law for Swiss Federal Supreme Court case law from 2000 onward plus user-imported corpora, beating simple semantic-map baselines in legal usefulness.

corpus.question: When 174k artifact publishing + embedding compute budget confirmed: publish full 174,113-decision normalized corpus artifacts (parquet/JSONL) with schema validation, citation ID resolution, and field coverage ground truth; enable downstream lanes to compute embeddings at full-corpus scale.

legal-distance.question: When 174k artifacts available: (1) run full-corpus adversarial evaluation at 174k scale on all production representations, (2) section-specific cross-lingual evaluation (sachverhalt/erwaegungen/dispositiv) at full corpus density, (3) scale linear_hybrid05_concat stability test at 174k, (4) re-test production-deployment vs CV tradeoff at 174k density to resolve TF-IDF SVD information-leakage hypothesis.

fractal-map.question: When 174k artifacts published + compute budget confirmed: scale all 29+ validated representations to full 174k corpus using compressed 5-level resolution ladder [0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0], validate citation-role zoom quality at 174k, and implement multi-view zoom UI with citation role views per accepted fractal-map audit recommendation.

evaluation.question: When 174k artifacts published + jurist recruitment complete: (1) run full 12-benchmark formal suite at 174k scale on all production representations, (2) execute jurist human study (framework ready, needs 5-10 Swiss jurists), (3) validate citation_heritage benchmark (requires 174k citation-ID resolution), (4) test whether v17b label normalization (15-25% purity gain, reproduced 4 seeds) generalizes to 174k fine-grained legal_area labels.

product.question: When 174k corpus artifacts delivered: switch product from synthetic-scale simulation to real 174k data — wire production defaults to full-corpus artifacts, validate 54 API endpoints at 174k scale, and confirm section coverage, LOD/culling/WebGL pipeline performance at production load.
